web.title: Hair dryer brush / hot air brush — Grokipedia

lead: A hot air brush, also called a hair dryer brush or blow-dry brush, is a handheld styling tool that combines a brush with heated airflow so that hair can be dried, smoothed and given volume in one pass. Models such as the Revlon One-Step are commonly named examples [1].

Descriptions of the tool come mainly from consumer-review-style sources rather than clinical research. Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia that cites product testers, says hot air brushes are particularly used for root lift and body on fine hair, and that testers report faster drying than a separate dryer and round brush [1]. No published clinical studies of hot air brushes were found.
infobox: Revlon One-Step Volumizer; Dyson Airwrap (as named by Grokipedia) [1]
Ionic technology, adjustable heat and airflow, rotating or oval barrels [1]

paras: The device has a motor that draws air over a heating element and out through vents in a brush head, and Grokipedia describes the bristles lifting hair at the roots while the airflow dries it [1]. Some models add ionic technology that is said to reduce static and frizz, and some offer rotating barrels or multiple attachments [1].

Claims about volume, time savings and reduced heat damage versus flat irons are made by product testers and manufacturers [1]. No independent study measuring these outcomes was found, so they remain untested in the published literature.

No research specific to hot air brushes was found. As with other heated styling tools, heat exposure to hair and scalp is the main consideration, and general sources note that overuse of heat tools can damage hair.
